```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Raigani et al. (2017) developed a mutated chimeric tissue plasminogen activator
(mt-PA) by deleting the finger, EGF and kringle-1 domains of wild-type t-PA,
inserting a GHRP fibrin-binding tetrapeptide, and substituting the KHRR 296-299
residues with four alanines to confer resistance to plasminogen activator
inhibitor-1. They characterised its plasma fibrinolytic-activity pharmacokinetics
in female Wistar rats after single intravenous bolus doses, with wild-type
Alteplase as the comparator. Plasma activity decayed biphasically and was fit to
a two-compartment model. This paper contributes two model files, both built here:

* **mt-PA** -- `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Raigani_2017_mtpa_rat"))$description`
* **Alteplase** -- `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Raigani_2017_alteplase_rat"))$description`

Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Raigani_2017_mtpa_rat"))$reference`

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/srep43028>

# Population

The study used female Wistar rats (12-14 weeks, 230-250 g) from the Pasteur
Institute of Iran. mt-PA was given as a single tail-vein i.v. bolus at 100 IU
(3 rats), 200 IU (4 rats) or 400 IU (6 rats) in 0.5 mL; Alteplase was given at
4000 IU (6 rats) as a positive control. Plasma fibrinolytic activity was measured
by an amidolytic (Chromolize t-PA) assay before and at 2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 45,
60, 75, 90 and 120 min after mt-PA, and before and at 2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30 and
45 min after Alteplase (Methods, "Preparation and administration of dosing
solution"; Table 1). Because the assay reports fibrinolytic activity, doses and
concentrations are expressed in international units (IU) rather than mass, and no
molar amount or body-weight normalisation is defined.

The population metadata are available programmatically, e.g.
`readModelDb("Raigani_2017_mtpa_rat")()$population`.

# Source trace

The authors fit plasma activity to the bi-exponential
`Cp(t) = D * (A * exp(-alpha * t) + B * exp(-beta * t))` (Eq. 1), reporting the
macro-constants A, B, alpha and beta per treatment/dose group in Table 3, with
log-additive covariate effects for treatment and mt-PA dose (Eq. 7). mt-PA dose
was not statistically significant across the three doses (Table 3), so the single
mt-PA parameter set here is the pooled mt-PA estimate (Alteplase reference shifted
by the mt-PA treatment coefficient). The macro-constants were converted to
canonical CL/Vc/Q/Vp by the standard bi-exponential relationships
(`Vc = 1/(A+B)`; `k21 = (A*beta + B*alpha)/(A+B)`; `k10 = alpha*beta/k21`;
`k12 = alpha+beta-k21-k10`; `CL = k10*Vc`; `Q = k12*Vc`; `Vp = Q/k21`), which
reproduce the micro-constants and volumes reported directly in Table 1.

| Model | Parameter | Value | Source location |
|-------|-----------|-------|-----------------|
| mt-PA | macro-constants (pooled) | A=0.01249, B=0.005231 /mL; alpha=0.3694, beta=0.03041 /min | Table 3 (Alteplase reference + mt-PA coefficients), Eq. 7 |
| mt-PA | `CL` | 4.86 mL/min | Derived; cf. Table 1 CLp 3.9-5.9 mL/min |
| mt-PA | `Vc` | 56.4 mL | Derived; cf. Table 1 V1 48.3-58.7 mL |
| mt-PA | `Q` | 10.34 mL/min | Derived from Table 3 |
| mt-PA | `Vp` | 79.3 mL | Derived; cf. Table 1 V2 42.9-105.2 mL |
| Alteplase | macro-constants | A=0.00176, B=0.000191 /mL; alpha=0.383, beta=0.0811 /min | Table 3 (Dose=4000, reference) |
| Alteplase | `CL` | 143.88 mL/min | Derived; cf. Table 1 CLp 142.6 mL/min |
| Alteplase | `Vc` | 512.6 mL | Derived; cf. Table 1 V1 509.3 mL |
| Alteplase | `Q` | 37.28 mL/min | Derived from Table 3 |
| Alteplase | `Vp` | 336.9 mL | Derived; cf. Table 1 V2 328.7 mL |
| both | `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | n/a | Standard 2-compartment i.v.-bolus disposition, Eq. 1 |
| both | `propSd` | fixed 0 | No residual error model reported (least-squares fit) |

# Simulation

Both models are typical-value only (no inter-individual variance or residual
error was reported), so the profiles below are deterministic. Each dose scenario
is a single i.v. bolus into the central compartment, observed on the paper's
sampling grid extended to a 1-minute resolution for clean NCA.

```{r simulate}
mod_mt <- readModelDb("Raigani_2017_mtpa_rat")
mod_al <- readModelDb("Raigani_2017_alteplase_rat")

obs_t <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, 120, by = 1),
  c(2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90, 120)
)))

sim_one <- function(mod, dose, label, id) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose, cmt = "central") |>
    rxode2::et(obs_t)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = id, treatment = label, dose = dose)
}

sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_one(mod_mt, 100, "mt-PA 100 IU", 1L),
  sim_one(mod_mt, 200, "mt-PA 200 IU", 2L),
  sim_one(mod_mt, 400, "mt-PA 400 IU", 3L),
  sim_one(mod_al, 4000, "Alteplase 4000 IU", 4L)
)
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
# Replicates Figure 4(a-d) of Raigani 2017: plasma activity vs time, semi-log,
# for each mt-PA dose and Alteplase.
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0, Cc > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)", y = "Plasma activity Cc (IU/mL)",
    title = "Figure 4 - plasma activity-time profiles",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4(a-d) of Raigani 2017."
  )
```

```{r figure-4e, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates Figure 4e of Raigani 2017: 400 IU mt-PA vs 4000 IU Alteplase.
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment %in% c("mt-PA 400 IU", "Alteplase 4000 IU"),
                time > 0, Cc > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)", y = "Plasma activity Cc (IU/mL)",
    colour = NULL,
    title = "Figure 4e - mt-PA 400 IU vs Alteplase 4000 IU",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4e of Raigani 2017."
  )
```

The longer terminal phase of mt-PA (elimination half-life ~23 min) relative to
Alteplase (~8.5 min) reproduces the paper's central finding.

# PKNCA validation

NCA is run per treatment group and compared against the compartmental parameters
tabulated in Table 1. For an i.v. bolus the time-zero record is the post-bolus
concentration, so no defensive time-zero row is needed here.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)

dose_df <- sim |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, dose) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0) |>
  dplyr::rename(amt = dose)

dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start      = 0,
  end        = Inf,
  cmax       = TRUE,
  aucinf.obs = TRUE,
  half.life  = TRUE,
  cl.obs     = TRUE,
  mrt.obs    = TRUE,
  vss.obs    = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Table 1 reports AUC0->inf, elimination half-life, plasma clearance (CLp), mean
residence time (MRT) and steady-state volume (Vss) per dose group. These are the
NCA/compartmental summaries the simulated profiles should reproduce.

```{r nca_compare}
# Transcribed from Table 1 (Mean values per group).
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,          ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life, ~cl.obs, ~mrt.obs, ~vss.obs,
  "mt-PA 100 IU",      17.0,        20.3,       5.9,     23.3,     137.6,
  "mt-PA 200 IU",      59.2,        19.1,       3.9,     25.4,     91.2,
  "mt-PA 400 IU",      83.3,        26.1,       5.4,     31.8,     163.9,
  "Alteplase 4000 IU", 28.3,        8.3,        142.6,   6.0,      838.0
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by        = "treatment",
  units     = c(aucinf.obs = "IU*min/mL", half.life = "min",
                cl.obs = "mL/min", mrt.obs = "min", vss.obs = "mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)

knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated vs. published NCA (Table 1). * differs from reference by >20%.",
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r")
)
```

The dose-independent disposition parameters (half-life, CLp, MRT, Vss) match
Table 1 closely for both drugs. The pooled mt-PA model enforces exact
dose-proportionality of AUC, so AUC0->inf agrees for the 100 IU and 400 IU groups
but under-predicts the 200 IU group, whose observed mean AUC (59.2 +/- 23.9) is
higher than a proportional scaling of the 100 IU value (17.0 +/- 1.6) would give.
This reflects the large between-animal scatter at small sample sizes rather than a
true dose effect: Raigani 2017 tested dose as a covariate with a Wald test and
found no significant difference among the three mt-PA doses (Table 3), which is
why the three groups are pooled here. No parameters were tuned to the Table 1
values.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Pooled mt-PA dose groups.** mt-PA dose was not a significant covariate on the
  disposition macro-constants (Table 3), so the three mt-PA dose groups are
  represented by one parameter set (the Alteplase reference shifted by the mt-PA
  treatment coefficient, Eq. 7). The consequence is exact dose-proportional AUC,
  which under-predicts the (highly variable, n = 4) observed 200 IU AUC; this is
  documented above and not corrected by tuning.
- **Two separate model files.** mt-PA and Alteplase were fit jointly in one
  regression with treatment as the reference-level covariate, but they are two
  distinct molecules with independent disposition parameters, so the maintainers
  packaged them as two model files (`Raigani_2017_mtpa_rat`,
  `Raigani_2017_alteplase_rat`) sharing this one vignette.
- **Canonical CL/Vc/Q/Vp from reported macro-constants.** The paper estimated the
  bi-exponential macro-constants (A, B, alpha, beta; Table 3); the canonical
  clearances and volumes were derived from them by the standard two-compartment
  relationships and cross-checked against the micro-constants and volumes
  reported directly in Table 1.
- **No inter-individual or residual variability.** The fit was a nonlinear
  least-squares regression; individual-animal spread appears only graphically
  (Figure 5) and was not reported as variance components, and no residual error
  model was reported. Both models are therefore typical-value only, with the
  proportional residual error fixed at zero.
- **Activity units.** All amounts and concentrations are in IU of fibrinolytic
  activity, as measured by the amidolytic assay; the models carry no mass or
  molar interpretation and no per-kilogram scaling.
- No correction or erratum notice for this article was found as of 2026-11-25.
```
